description: List orders (material/item requests) in the organization, newest first, grouped by active vs closed. Order managers see all orders; other members see only orders they requested or are assigned to (the result field `isManager` tells you which view you got). Each order row: id, status, requester, deliver-to target, the free-text request, the requested lines (a specific item, any instance of a model (`modelId`), any item of a category (`categoryId`), or free text; each with its `quantity` where one was given — "5 Packungen Kopierpapier" is quantity 5), `neededByAt` (when the requester needs it, absent when they did not say) and the assignee. Every date comes twice — the epoch and its ISO twin: `neededByAtIso` is a plain calendar day ("2026-08-11"), `createdAtIso` / `closedAtIso` are UTC instants. Read the ISO one to your user; this server does no timezone conversion, so never re-zone a calendar day. Status values: "open" = requested, nobody has started fulfilling it; "in_fulfillment" = an order manager is working on it; "fulfilled" (delivered), "rejected" (declined by a manager) and "cancelled" (withdrawn by the requester) are closed. Filter with `status`, or omit it to get all orders — "open orders" in the everyday sense usually means open + in_fulfillment. `status` scopes the READS themselves, so it genuinely reaches older orders of that status instead of narrowing an already-capped page. An order has no printed code and its `id` is a machine handle for your next call — when you name an order to your user, give them the `webUrl` link with the requester and the request text, never the raw id. If the result field `truncated` is true the organization has more orders than returned — do not treat the list as complete. The caps: the newest 100 per ACTIVE status (open, in_fulfillment), the newest 50 per CLOSED status (fulfilled, rejected, cancelled), and the closed rows are then cut to 50 in total. Narrowing with `status` is what actually gets you past them.

status.description: Only return orders with this status (omit to return all)

name: list_orders

isManager.description: False means you only see your own orders

closedAtIso.description: When the order was closed, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp

createdAtIso.description: When the order was placed, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp

neededByAt.description: When the requester needs it, epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight. Absent when they did not say

neededByAtIso.description: The needed-by date as a plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD" — read THIS one. A DAY, not a moment: the server does no timezone conversion, so do not re-zone it

requestedItems.description: Requested lines: an item, a model (any instance), a category (any item in it) or free text

categoryId.description: Category line: any item of this category, subcategories included — the store picks which

modelId.description: Model line: any instance of this model — the store picks which

name.description: Name of the requested item, model or category as it was when ordered

quantity.description: How many were asked for on that line ("5 Packungen Kopierpapier" = 5). Absent when the requester named no amount — on BOTH item and free-text lines

webUrl.description: Link to the order in the web app — give your user THIS, never the raw `id`

truncated.description: A bounded read hit its cap

title: List orders
